findings.title: Belief tested by assigned authority and boundary status
findings.claim: The focus counterfactual can make belief legible through the authority and support a group assigns, while the closing boundary image presents the actors as emerging from a professed containment.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers for adopted authority and support meet the conditional belief relation, while the focus boundary carrier is connected by the supplied 5:59 relation between belief, delivered revelation, and fasiqun. That contact changes the reading from an isolated social preference to an allegiance test with a boundary consequence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the conditional form links inward assent to the external relation being empowered, and why the final diagnosis adds a boundary image rather than merely repeating a group label.
findings.containment: The focus branch facets are supplied lexical records; the wider connection rows provide target Arabic but no target morphology. The emergence image remains a qualified contextual resonance, and it does not claim that every form of proximity has this force or that the boundary image supplies a strict causal sequence.

epistemic.reason: The focus carriers and branch facets are explicit, but the reader-walk source is legacy-unbound and the wider connection evidence is review provenance rather than a focus-direction verdict.

findings.title: A rival binding sequence
findings.claim: The focus adoption of awliyāʾ can be read as installing a rival binding sequence in which chosen proximity organizes whom desire follows after the covenant-message sequence loses practical control.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers for acquiring, taking, and continuous succession meet attributed contextual carriers for covenant, inward desire, following, exited obedience, and failed restraint across 5:70 and 5:77-5:79. Their contact changes the focus from an isolated alliance choice into a possible substitution between governing chains.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the focus allegiance against a prior binding relation: the question becomes which sequence holds conduct, rather than only whom people call allies.
findings.containment: The focus branch facets are supplied; every contextual role is attributed from a legacy-unbound HFT trace. The packet keeps open the alternative that alliance is a downstream symptom of covenant failure rather than its replacement, and it does not assert a strict causal order.

epistemic.reason: Exact focus carriers and attributed contextual coordinates support the relation, but contextual branch records are unresolved and the source identity is legacy-unbound.
